transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because… I don’t know how else to put it, but most days it feels like I’m sitting at the bottom of a dark hole. It’s heavy, like it’s just pressing down on me all the time, and I can’t seem to get out from under it. Even when I’m around people I know, people I should feel comfortable with, it doesn’t really lift. I still feel alone in it, and hopeless, like nothing is going to change. That’s what finally made me come in.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things the way you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once cared about?

Yeah… very much. That’s actually one of the things that scares me, because I used to have a lot of things I cared about. I used to love hiking—like, I’d plan a whole weekend around getting out somewhere, even just a familiar trail, because being out there felt like it reset something in me. And I used to paint, too. I’ve still got supplies sitting there, brushes and half-used tubes and canvases, and I’ll look at them and think, “I should do something,” but then I just… stare at it, and it feels like too much effort to even start.

I also used to go to the makerspace and tinker with stuff. That was kind of my place, you know? I liked fixing things, figuring out how to make something work, messing around with tools. Even at work, if there was a tricky install, I used to get this little spark from solving it, like, okay, let me work through this. Now it all just feels flat. Like there’s no payoff in it. People will call or text about going out or doing something, and I ignore it because I can’t make myself care enough to respond, even though part of me knows I used to want those things.

It’s not that I suddenly hate hiking or painting or fixing things. It’s more like none of it feels worth starting anymore.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yes. Most days, it’s there for the majority of the day. I wake up and it’s like it’s already waiting for me, this heavy, dark feeling, and I carry it through the day. It’s not just a bad mood that comes and goes, or something that lifts if I get busy or talk to someone.

Even when I’m around people I know, people who care about me, I still feel like I’m at the bottom of that hole. I can hear them talking and I can be sitting right there, but inside I just feel alone and hopeless, like nothing is really going to change. It’s been going on long enough that I stopped thinking, “Maybe tomorrow will be better,” because most days it just feels the same.
Have you felt unusually tired or have you noticed a lack of energy most days?

I’m… honestly not sure how to answer that. I haven’t really been paying attention to it as “tired,” exactly. Some days I feel slowed down or like everything takes more out of me than it should, but I don’t know if that’s the same as being unusually tired or having no energy.

It’s more like I notice the heaviness first, if that makes sense. I’m not waking up thinking, “Oh, I’m exhausted,” the way I would after a long workday or bad sleep. I just kind of… have trouble getting myself moving. But I can’t say I’ve clearly noticed being physically tired most days. I guess I’d say I’m not sure.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to think clearly, concentrate, or make decisions lately?

Yes… definitely. That’s been happening a lot, and it’s honestly embarrassing because it’s with stuff I used to be able to do without even thinking.

Like at work, paperwork and repair diagrams used to be second nature to me. I could look at a diagram, follow what went where, figure out the next step, fill out whatever form I needed, and just keep moving. Now I’ll have the same papers in front of me and they kind of blur together. I don’t mean my eyesight, exactly, I mean my brain just won’t sort it out. I’ll read the same line over and over and it doesn’t seem to stick.

And decision-making has gotten ridiculous. I’ll sit there stuck on something so small, like which form to open first, or what part of the diagram I should start with, and it feels like my mind just locks up. Then I get frustrated because I know I know how to do this. It’s not new to me. But in the moment it feels like trying to think through mud.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating much less or much more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Yeah… my eating has been really off. It’s not like I’m following any kind of diet or trying to change anything, it’s just… I don’t eat normally anymore.

A lot of days I’ll get through most of the day on coffee. I’ll think I should eat something, but then when I actually look at food or think about making something, my stomach kind of turns. It’s not even that I’m making a decision not to eat, exactly. It just feels unappealing, like food is too much somehow.

Then later at night, when everything is quiet, I’ll end up standing in the kitchen and picking at whatever’s in the cabinet. Crackers, cereal, whatever is there. But I’m not really enjoying it or tasting it. It’s more like I’m just putting something in my mouth because I realize I barely ate all day, or because I don’t know what else to do with myself.

As far as weight, I haven’t been keeping close track of it. I just know my appetite is not normal for me right now.
Have you found yourself feeling worthless or guilty about things you’ve done—or haven’t done—lately?

Yeah… I have. A lot. It’s actually hard to say out loud because it sounds dramatic, but in my head it’s constant.

I keep telling myself I’m useless now, like… if I can’t work the way I used to, then what am I even good for? I’ve always been someone who could fix things, figure things out, show up, pull my weight. That was kind of the one thing I could count on about myself. And now when I can’t keep up or I mess something up or I freeze on something I should know, I don’t just think, “I’m having a bad day.” I go straight to, “You’re useless. You’re letting everyone down.”

And the guilt just loops. I think about apprentices I’ve worked with, people I was supposed to teach or look out for, and I start replaying every time I was short with them, or didn’t explain something well, or wasn’t as available as I should’ve been. Even if it was a small thing, my brain turns it into proof that I failed them.

Same with bills. If something’s unpaid or late, I can’t just see it as a bill. It feels like evidence that I’ve ruined everything, like I’ve somehow wrecked my whole life by not being able to stay on top of things. I’ll sit there going over it again and again, like there’s some trial happening in my head and every little mistake is another piece of proof against me.

I know some of it probably sounds over the top when I say it out loud, but when I’m in it, it feels completely true.
Have you had any thoughts about death or dying, or have you thought about hurting yourself?

Yeah… I have. I don’t like saying that, but yes.

It’s not every second like I’m planning something out, but I do have thoughts like… people would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. Like if I went to sleep and that was it, maybe it would be easier for everyone. That thought has been coming up more than I want to admit.

And sometimes when everything piles up — the pain, the money worries, feeling like I can’t get anything straightened out — I catch myself thinking about ending it. Not just “I’m tired,” but actually like… what if I didn’t have to keep doing this anymore. And that scares me. It scares me that my mind even goes there, because part of me doesn’t want to think that way, but when I’m in it, it feels like I’m boxed in and I can’t see another way out.

I haven’t really wanted to tell anyone because it sounds awful, and I don’t want people looking at me like I’m dangerous or crazy or something. But yes… those thoughts have been there.

Have you ever felt this way before—like you were stuck in a dark hole, lost interest in things, and had thoughts about death or hurting yourself—or is this the first time you’ve experienced something like this?

It’s… this time has been the real thing, I guess. I mean, I’ve had hard periods before like anybody, times where I was stressed or down, but not like this.

This has been going on about a year and two months now. It started after that fall on the HVAC job, when I hurt my back. That’s kind of the line in my mind—before that and after that. After the injury, it felt like everything started unraveling one piece at a time, and I never really got my footing back.

At first I kept telling myself it was temporary, like, “Okay, you’re hurt, you’re frustrated, you’ll heal and get back to normal.” But the longer it went on, the darker everything got. So no, this isn’t something that’s been happening my whole life in this same way. It’s been since that fall, and it’s been going on for over a year now.
